newsitem.title: USA: US Customs head urges private, public cooperation.
newsitem.headline: US Customs head urges private, public cooperation.

text.p: U.S. Customs Service Commissioner George Weise Monday called for more cooperation between governments and private sector entities to standardize and speed customs procedures.

"Cooperation between the trade, investors and customs administrators" is the only way for free trade to flourish, Weise told 1,000 international delegates gathered at the Customs/Trade/Finance Symposium of the Americas in Miami.
Customs should be involved in any trade negotiations from the beginning, Weise said.
"We can alert the policy-makers when we see them going in directions that we know from our own hard experience won't work at the point of administration," Weise said.

U.S. Customs has been working for four years to enhance its automation and work with the private sector to eliminate the transaction-by-transaction approach in favor of an account approach, Weise said.
"Today we are putting account managers into place so that major importers can have one contact within customs," Weise said.
Weise said that the U.S., Canadian and Mexican customs have already cultivated a relationship with their counterparts in Chile.

"Should negotiation of Chilean ascension to NAFTA become a reality, we will be working very closely with Chilean customs to ensure a high level of cooperation between all of the NAFTA partners, present and future."
Another speaker, James Shaver, secretary general of the World Customs Organization, Brussels told of the success of Peru's customs reform over the last five years.

"They have had amazing results. They have cut their clearance time from five days to two hours, cut tariffs dramatically and yet revenues are up dramatically. They have gone from 100 percent physical inspection to less than 15 percent."
